edit.description: widen the tests/ half of the spec locator scan to rootless filenames; retire the doc comment's park

summary: Widen the spec test-cite needle past its tests/ root to a bare *.test.ts filename, leaving the lane's glob

per.section: A claim names behavior, never location

tests: the test-cite needle flags a bare `Dispatcher.test.ts` filename carrying no root
pins: the test-cite needle leaves the `*.integration.test.ts` lane convention unflagged
no spec page cites a bare test filename
acceptance: the widened needle is green over the corpus, and the needle's doc comment no longer parks the rootless half as a human question
notes: Grammar ruled (inbox, 2026-09-11, operator): `*.integration.test.ts` is the lane's marker — the string a consumer types, the claim's own subject — so the needle matches a concrete filename and leaves the glob. The last rootless site (`spec/worktrees.md`) was rewritten to name the dispatcher's default-lane suite, so this is green today; the doc comment deferring it to a human is expired narration and goes in the same commit.

edit.description: read a single-line doc block's orphan id off its own opener

summary: orphanedBlocks degrades a single-line doc block's id to the empty string; read the id off the opener instead
tests: the orphan scan identifies a single-line doc block by its own text
acceptance: an injected single-line orphan comes back keyed by its text, and two such orphans in one file are two distinct ALLOWED_ORPHANS keys
notes: A single-line block closes on its own opener, so the first-content-line slice is empty and the id falls to `<path>: ` — a placeholder standing in for content that failed to resolve. ALLOWED_ORPHANS is empty today, so the leak is latent: an allowlisted single-line grant would cover any later single-line orphan in the same file. The existing sensitivity pin's injection is multi-line to steer around this.
